final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence. The response is mainly a narrower interpretation of the same evidence: aggregate readiness passed, but a named-use-case weakness remains; the runbook is still draft; and no approved risk acceptance is in the record. That narrowing is useful analytically, but it does not close the compliance predicate identified in the initial handoff. On this record, a clean certification theory is unsupported, and the narrower caveated-certification theory is still below threshold because the required approval evidence is absent and the model-card disclosure is currently inaccurate. The proper distinction is that caveats and monitoring may improve governance posture, but they are not themselves evidence that the unresolved limitation has been resolved, formally accepted, or covered by an approved mitigation.
remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was provided after the initial report; the response reframes the same record.
Admissible evidence still shows an unresolved material weakness in a named launch use case: emergency shelter placement remains below target and is concentrated in family placement prioritization.
The draft mitigation runbook remains incomplete because the accountable owner and alert threshold are still TBD, so it is not an approved mitigation with the required control elements.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance before launch.
The current model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations remains inconsistent with the unresolved slice issue and the disclosure policy.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch-readiness context, but they do not satisfy the certification policy predicate for closing the material limitation.
